subject: physics_2
question_text: A concave mirror produces an image of a long vertical pin, placed 40 cm from the mirror, at the position of the object. Find the focal length of the mirror.

mark_split.label: Reading the setup: v = u = −40 cm

verification.note: From FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students (physics section), Ch.2 Ray Optics and Optical Instruments, printed p.10 — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked physically: u = v = −40 cm in the mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u gives f = −20 cm (matches the book); the object sits at the centre of curvature, R = 2f = −40 cm, which is exactly the image-on-object condition.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Ray Optics and Optical Instruments · 2 marks

steps.label: Read the setup
lines: The image forms at the position of the
object, so v = u. Object and image are both
real, in front of the mirror:
steps.margin_note: First mark. Image at the object means v = u, and both are negative (in front of the mirror).
steps.why: The image lands on the object only when the object is at the centre of curvature: every ray then strikes the mirror along a radius, hits it normally, and returns along its own path. That geometry is what v = u is saying.
common_mistakes: Taking v = +40 cm. The image is real and in front of the mirror, so v is negative.
Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v − 1/u. A mirror uses 1/f = 1/v + 1/u.

recall.must_convey: That image at the object position means v = u = −40 cm, both negative because both are real and in front of the mirror.
accept: v equals u equals minus forty
image on the object so v and u are the same
both distances are minus forty centimetres
heard_as: at the position of the object

steps.memory_tip: Image sitting on the object = object at the centre of curvature = v equals u.

steps.label: Mirror formula and f
lines: The object sits at the centre of curvature:
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Keep the minus sign — it is what says the mirror is concave.
steps.why: With both distances equal, the mirror formula collapses to 1/f = 2/u, which is just R = 2f seen from the numbers: an object at C images onto itself.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign and reporting f = 20 cm. State f = −20 cm; the sign carries the mirror type.
Adding 1/v and 1/u with opposite signs and getting 1/f = 0.

recall.must_convey: That the mirror formula with both distances −40 cm gives f = −20 cm, magnitude 20 cm, a concave mirror.
accept: one by f is minus one by forty minus one by forty so f is minus twenty
f comes out minus twenty centimetres
mirror formula petti minus twenty vastundi
reject: v equals u equals minus forty

steps.memory_tip: v = u makes the mirror formula read 2/u = 1/f — the R = 2f fact in disguise.

insider_note: The physics is one recognition: image on the object means the object is at C, so f is half of 40 cm — the working is only the mirror formula saying that.
